entities.commonMisinterpretations: Assuming higher threat always increases protective action; low efficacy can instead produce denial, avoidance, or paralysis.
entities.definition: The belief that one can deploy effective cognitive, emotional, or behavioral responses to manage a specified stressor.
entities.evidenceNotes: Scientifically defensible with substantial supporting literature, while causal identification, construct boundaries, measurement, or transferability remain context dependent. Representative records: SRC111; SRC121.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Threat- and coping-appraisal scales; probability/severity elicitation; scenario tasks; repeated state assessment
entities.measurementCaveats: Appraisals are domain- and time-specific and may diverge from objective hazard, actual skill, or actual control.
entities.mechanism: Supports engagement and adaptive coping while reducing helpless or avoidant responses.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Response efficacy, personal capability, immediacy, uncertainty, prior experience, and resource availability.
entities.name: Coping Self-Efficacy
entities.persistenceRecovery: Often persists for days to months; updating depends on counterevidence and confidence.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater perceived ability to cope effectively.

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Assuming higher threat always increases protective action; low efficacy can instead produce denial, avoidance, or paralysis.
entities.definition: The judged ease or difficulty of performing a specified behavior, including perceived control over internal and external constraints.
entities.evidenceNotes: Supported by established theory, validated measures, and converging review, meta-analytic, experimental, or longitudinal evidence. Magnitude and behavioral direction remain conditional on context. Representative records: SRC110; SRC107.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Threat- and coping-appraisal scales; probability/severity elicitation; scenario tasks; repeated state assessment
entities.measurementCaveats: Appraisals are domain- and time-specific and may diverge from objective hazard, actual skill, or actual control.
entities.mechanism: Shapes intention and can predict action when it tracks actual control.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Response efficacy, personal capability, immediacy, uncertainty, prior experience, and resource availability.
entities.name: Perceived Behavioral Control
entities.persistenceRecovery: Usually reversible as cues, resources, or interpretations change; repeated appraisal can stabilize.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater perceived control or ease.
entities.representationScale: Very difficult–very easy; no control–complete control

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Assuming higher threat always increases protective action; low efficacy can instead produce denial, avoidance, or paralysis.
entities.definition: The judged degree to which a specified situation or outcome can be influenced by one's actions or available responses.

entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Threat- and coping-appraisal scales; probability/severity elicitation; scenario tasks; repeated state assessment
entities.measurementCaveats: Appraisals are domain- and time-specific and may diverge from objective hazard, actual skill, or actual control.
entities.mechanism: Changes coping selection, effort, stress appraisal, and willingness to act.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Response efficacy, personal capability, immediacy, uncertainty, prior experience, and resource availability.
entities.name: Perceived Controllability
entities.persistenceRecovery: Usually reversible as cues, resources, or interpretations change; repeated appraisal can stabilize.
entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater perceived ability to influence the situation or outcome.

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Assuming higher threat always increases protective action; low efficacy can instead produce denial, avoidance, or paralysis.
entities.definition: The degree to which a person expects that their actions will not meaningfully influence important outcomes in a specified context.
entities.evidenceNotes: Scientifically defensible with substantial supporting literature, while causal identification, construct boundaries, measurement, or transferability remain context dependent. Representative records: SRC109; SRC122.
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Threat- and coping-appraisal scales; probability/severity elicitation; scenario tasks; repeated state assessment
entities.measurementCaveats: Appraisals are domain- and time-specific and may diverge from objective hazard, actual skill, or actual control.
entities.mechanism: Reduces initiation and persistence by weakening expected action–outcome contingency.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Response efficacy, personal capability, immediacy, uncertainty, prior experience, and resource availability.
entities.name: Perceived Helplessness

entities.polarityDirection: Higher values = greater expected ineffectiveness of personal action.

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Assuming higher threat always increases protective action; low efficacy can instead produce denial, avoidance, or paralysis.
entities.definition: The subjective probability that a specified adverse or beneficial outcome will occur under stated conditions.

entities.measurementCaveats: Appraisals are domain- and time-specific and may diverge from objective hazard, actual skill, or actual control.

entities.measurementCaveats: Appraisals are domain- and time-specific and may diverge from objective hazard, actual skill, or actual control.

entities.commonMisinterpretations: Do not treat Subjective Uncertainty as interchangeable with PSY-131; INF-015; PSY-116 or as a universal, context-free cause.
entities.definition: Current perceived lack of confidence about relevant states, causes, outcomes, or probabilities.
entities.evidenceNotes: A dynamic perceived-uncertainty state is distinct from PSY-131 intolerance of uncertainty and INF-015 disclosure.
indicators: Construct-valid indicators of subjective uncertainty measured for the specified unit, setting, and reference period
entities.measurementAssessmentMethods: Use a validated construct-specific instrument, administrative or sensor measure, or transparent composite with explicit unit and reference period.
entities.measurementCaveats: Feasible With Explicit Unit; proxy measures require construct-validity review.
entities.mechanism: State uncertainty changes search, vigilance, delay, reliance on authorities, and susceptibility to closure cues.
entities.moderatorsBoundaryConditions: Interpret only for the specified population, unit, setting, exposure, reference period, and measurement method; effects may vary across contexts.
entities.name: Subjective Uncertainty
entities.persistenceRecovery: Persistence and recovery depend on exposure, baseline state, intervention, and system feedback.
entities.representationScale: Continuous or ordinal construct-specific measure with population, setting, reference period, and unit explicitly specified.
entities.timeScaleQualifier: Typical state-change speed is context-dependent; do not infer persistence from this band.
